assumptions: An ABI clone borrows an existing counted source lease for the duration of acquisition; source release consumes a distinct unborrowed owner. This ownership transfer is modeled explicitly.

Atomic count RMWs follow one modification order. Reads may return any prior modification, an overapproximation of coherent stale reads; no cross-object sequentially consistent order is assumed for count and retired.

The model proves arbitrary interleavings of borrow, load, CAS success/retry/overflow, source release, retired observation, zero observation and image take. The successful RMWs are count linearization points.

The source probe executes exact count, retired, reap, acquire and release bodies with real atomic/Arc/HashMap primitives. Dynamic library and cache destructors record invocation; operating-system unmapping is tested separately.

Rust pointer validity, the correctness of std atomics/Arc/mutex, valid foreign ABI calls and compiler semantics remain runtime contracts; the module does not encode all Rust or C++ language semantics.
The scheduler owns one mutable Future poll at a time and preserves notifications emitted during that poll. The model separates Pending, Ready, cancellation, native destruction and permit return.

FairCleanup requires every nonterminal suffix eventually to execute an enabled start, return the current callback, or publish terminal completion. It allows unbounded intervening pending polls and observer drops; permanent host rejection and nonterminating callbacks violate this explicit liveness contract.

The rank counts each unstarted callback twice, the active callback once and terminal publication once. Safety holds for arbitrary event traces; eventual LIFO completion uses the stated fairness/termination contract.
Real Future/Waker/Pin/Arc and exact Admitted/Permit bodies execute in the probe. Tokio's internal scheduler and foreign destructor implementation are external contracts.
